question.text: Per NISM Ch 2 and the SEBI (AIF) Regulations 2012 framework, which of the following AIF-type-to-Category mappings is CORRECT?

answer.text: VCF = Category III; PE Fund = Category I; Hedge Fund = Category II
All AIFs including VCF, PE, Debt, and Hedge belong to Category I
Only Hedge Funds qualify as AIFs; VCFs and PE Funds are treated as mutual funds
VCF = Category I; Debt Fund / PE Fund = Category II; Hedge Fund = Category III

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per the SEBI (AIF) Regulations framework referenced across Ch 2, Category I houses funds with positive-externality strategies including VCFs, Social Venture Funds, Infrastructure Funds and SME Funds. Category II covers PE funds, debt funds and real estate PE that do not take leverage other than for operational needs. Category III covers hedge funds and funds using complex strategies and fund-level leverage. **The Trap:** Option A inverts every mapping. Option C collapses the three categories into one. Option D is factually wrong — VCFs and PE funds are explicit AIF sub-types. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-A tests Cat I/II only (distributor scope). XIX-B tests Cat III only. XIX-C uniquely unifies all three — this is a XIX-C-specific question style. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Before submitting an AIF application to SEBI, your strategy must map cleanly to one category. Dual-category ambitions (e.g., Cat II with hedge-fund-like tactical short positions) trigger a SEBI show-cause. Pick one category and design the PPM end-to-end around it.
